newsitem.title: USA: Cowen- Genzyme '97 EPS cut after management talks.
newsitem.headline: Cowen- Genzyme '97 EPS cut after management talks.

text.p: Cowen & Co lowered its 1997 earnings per share (EPS) on Genzyme Corp 20 cents to $1.20 after talks with management, analyst David Stone said in a telephone interview with Reuters.

Stone, who still rates the Cambridge, Mass. biotech firm a strong buy, said in his written comments about the company that he expects sales and EPS to accelerate in 1997 and has trimmed the 1998 estimate to $1.70. His one-year price target is $40-45 based on 25 times $1.70 1998 EPS.
Stone also issued EPS estimates for 1999 of $2.20 and $2.75 EPS for 2000.
Genzyme closed at 23-1/8 on Monday, off 2-3/8 points.

Stone expected sales of the firm's new surgical products, Seprafilm and Sepracoat, to begin to take off during the second half of 1997. Management has set a conservative revenue target of $125 million to $150 million for the surgical products unit, which includes Seprafilm and Sepracoat.

Stone said his bullish long-term outlook for the company is partially based on an ongoing interviews with surgeons and recent trends in the number of U.S. hospitals, which have bought at least small quantities of Seprafilm.
